question: How many shipments were cancelled last quarter?
ai_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS cancelled_shipments
FROM shipments
WHERE status = 'Cancelled'
  AND created_date BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30';
ai_answer: Last quarter, from July 1 to September 30, 2026, 946 shipments were cancelled. The count includes only shipments whose status is "Cancelled" and whose creation date falls within that period.

question: How many active shippers do we have per country?
ai_sql:
SELECT country,
       COUNT(*) AS active_shippers
FROM shippers
WHERE status = 'active'
GROUP BY country
ORDER BY country;
ai_answer: Active shippers are counted by country, with no date range applied; the filter is shippers whose status is active. Spain (ES) has 242, France (FR) has 235, Italy (IT) has 242, and the UK has 233. Spain and Italy are tied for the most active shippers, and the UK has the fewest.

question: What % of UK shipments were held at customs?
ai_sql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN s.hold_reason = 'At Customs' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS customs_hold_pct
FROM shipments s
JOIN shippers sh ON sh.shipper_id = s.shipper_id
WHERE sh.country = 'UK'
  AND s.status <> 'Cancelled';
ai_answer: Of UK shipments that were not cancelled, 8.5% were held at customs. The figure covers all non-cancelled shipments linked to UK shippers, with no date range applied, so it reflects the full period in the data. Cancelled shipments are excluded from the count.

question: Compare on-time rate and cost per package for milkrun vs direct, last quarter.
ai_sql:
WITH runs AS (
    SELECT run_id, run_type, cost_eur
    FROM truck_runs
    WHERE run_date BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'
),
run_cost AS (
    -- all runs in the period, including wasted runs
    SELECT run_type, SUM(cost_eur) AS total_cost
    FROM runs
    GROUP BY run_type
),
ship AS (
    SELECT r.run_type, s.promised_date, s.delivered_to_node_date, s.packages
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN runs r ON r.run_id = s.run_id
    WHERE s.status <> 'Cancelled'
),
ship_agg AS (
    SELECT run_type,
           COUNT(*) AS shipments,
           SUM(CASE WHEN delivered_to_node_date IS NOT NULL
                     AND delivered_to_node_date <= promised_date
                    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS on_time,
           SUM(packages) AS packages
    FROM ship
    GROUP BY run_type
)
SELECT sa.run_type,
       sa.shipments,
       ROUND(100.0 * sa.on_time / sa.shipments, 1) AS on_time_pct,
       ROUND(rc.total_cost, 2) AS total_cost_eur,
       sa.packages,
       ROUND(rc.total_cost / sa.packages, 2) AS cost_per_package_eur
FROM ship_agg sa
JOIN run_cost rc ON rc.run_type = sa.run_type
ORDER BY sa.run_type;
ai_answer: Direct runs were more reliable but cost more per package. From July 1 to September 30, 2026, direct runs delivered 87.8% of 47,300 shipments on time at €4.88 per package, while milkrun runs delivered 72.6% of 23,969 shipments on time at €2.67 per package. Cancelled shipments are left out of the on-time and package counts, but run costs include all runs in the period, including wasted ones.

question: What was our weekly attainment for FR shippers last quarter?
ai_sql:
WITH daily_actual AS (
    -- aggregate actual volume to shipper x pickup day BEFORE joining (no fan-out)
    SELECT s.shipper_id, tr.run_date AS pickup_date, SUM(s.packages) AS actual_packages
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = s.run_id
    WHERE s.status <> 'Cancelled'
    GROUP BY s.shipper_id, tr.run_date
),
fc AS (
    -- start from the forecast side; shipper country decides FR membership
    SELECT f.shipper_id,
           f.forecast_date,
           f.forecast_packages,
           date(f.forecast_date, '-' || strftime('%w', f.forecast_date) || ' days') AS week_start,
           COALESCE(a.actual_packages, 0) AS actual_packages
    FROM forecasts f
    JOIN shippers sh ON sh.shipper_id = f.shipper_id AND sh.country = 'FR'
    LEFT JOIN daily_actual a
      ON a.shipper_id = f.shipper_id AND a.pickup_date = f.forecast_date
)
SELECT week_start,
       SUM(actual_packages) AS actual_packages,
       SUM(forecast_packages) AS forecast_packages,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(actual_packages) / SUM(forecast_packages), 1) AS attainment_pct
FROM fc
WHERE week_start BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY week_start
ORDER BY week_start;
ai_answer: French shippers hit between 95.9% and 98.9% of forecast in every week from July through September 2026. The best week was the one starting July 5 (98.9%), and the lowest was the week starting August 16 (95.9%). The query counted only French shippers, excluded cancelled shipments, and grouped results into weeks starting Sunday. The final row (week starting September 27) covers only the days through September 30, so its totals are partial.

question: Which 10 shippers had the lowest attainment in Q3 2026?
ai_sql:
WITH daily_actual AS (
    -- aggregate actual volume to shipper x pickup day BEFORE joining (no fan-out)
    SELECT s.shipper_id, tr.run_date AS pickup_date, SUM(s.packages) AS actual_packages
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = s.run_id
    WHERE s.status <> 'Cancelled'
      AND tr.run_date BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'
    GROUP BY s.shipper_id, tr.run_date
),
q3_days AS (
    -- start from the forecast side; only days with a forecast row count
    SELECT f.shipper_id, f.forecast_date, f.forecast_packages,
           COALESCE(a.actual_packages, 0) AS actual_packages
    FROM forecasts f
    LEFT JOIN daily_actual a
      ON a.shipper_id = f.shipper_id AND a.pickup_date = f.forecast_date
    WHERE f.forecast_date BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'
)
SELECT q.shipper_id,
       sh.name,
       SUM(q.forecast_packages) AS forecast_packages,
       SUM(q.actual_packages) AS actual_packages,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(q.actual_packages) / SUM(q.forecast_packages), 1) AS attainment_pct
FROM q3_days q
JOIN shippers sh ON sh.shipper_id = q.shipper_id
GROUP BY q.shipper_id, sh.name
HAVING SUM(q.forecast_packages) >= 500
ORDER BY attainment_pct ASC
LIMIT 10;
ai_answer: The 10 shippers with the lowest attainment in Q3 2026 (July 1 to September 30) were all between 65.0% and 69.3% of forecast. The lowest was Turner, Ford and Dobson (S0087), at 65.0%, with 2,893 packages shipped against a forecast of 4,450. Cancelled shipments are excluded, and only shippers with at least 500 forecast packages in the quarter are included.

question: Did any de-listed shipper have volume after being de-listed?
ai_sql:
SELECT sh.shipper_id,
       sh.name,
       sh.delisted_date,
       SUM(s.packages) AS packages_after_delisting,
       COUNT(DISTINCT tr.run_id) AS runs_after_delisting,
       MAX(tr.run_date) AS last_pickup_date
FROM shippers sh
JOIN shipments s ON s.shipper_id = sh.shipper_id
JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = s.run_id
WHERE sh.status = 'de-listed'
  AND s.status <> 'Cancelled'
  AND tr.run_date > sh.delisted_date
GROUP BY sh.shipper_id, sh.name, sh.delisted_date
ORDER BY packages_after_delisting DESC;
ai_answer: No, none of the de-listed shippers had shipments picked up after their de-listing date. The check covered all shippers marked de-listed, counting only non-cancelled shipments with a truck run dated after each shipper's own de-listing date. Because the result is empty, no shipper appears in this list.

question: What was average truck utilisation by country last month?
ai_sql:
SELECT n.country,
       ROUND(1.0 * SUM(tr.pallets_loaded) / SUM(tr.pallet_capacity), 3) AS utilisation
FROM truck_runs tr
JOIN nodes n ON n.node_id = tr.node_id
WHERE tr.run_date BETWEEN '2026-09-01' AND '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY n.country
ORDER BY n.country;
ai_answer: In September 2026 (1 to 30 September), truck utilisation was very similar across all four countries. The UK was highest at 0.712, followed by ES at 0.710, IT at 0.709, and FR at 0.706, where 1.000 would mean full capacity. The figures combine all truck runs in each country during the month, weighting by pallet capacity rather than averaging each run equally.

question: Which nodes went over capacity during peak 2025, and on how many days?
ai_sql:
WITH daily_load AS (
    SELECT node_id, run_date, SUM(pallets_loaded) AS load_pallets
    FROM truck_runs
    WHERE run_date BETWEEN '2025-11-28' AND '2025-12-24'
    GROUP BY node_id, run_date
)
SELECT n.node_id,
       n.city,
       n.country,
       n.daily_capacity_pallets,
       COUNT(*) AS days_over_capacity,
       MAX(d.load_pallets) AS peak_day_load_pallets
FROM daily_load d
JOIN nodes n ON n.node_id = d.node_id
WHERE d.load_pallets > n.daily_capacity_pallets
GROUP BY n.node_id, n.city, n.country, n.daily_capacity_pallets
ORDER BY days_over_capacity DESC, peak_day_load_pallets DESC;
ai_answer: Only one node went over its daily capacity: London (node N-UK-01, UK), with 19 days over its limit of 150 pallets. Its busiest day reached 253 pallets. This covers 28 November to 24 December 2025, the period I counted as peak.

question: Which Account Managers' shippers drove the most avoidable cost last quarter?
ai_sql:
WITH run_avoidable AS (
    -- avoidable cost per run: full cost of wasted runs + ad-hoc premium
    SELECT tr.run_id,
           (CASE WHEN tr.run_outcome = 'wasted' THEN tr.cost_eur ELSE 0 END
          + CASE WHEN tr.is_adhoc = 1 THEN tr.cost_eur * 0.6 / 1.6 ELSE 0 END) AS avoidable
    FROM truck_runs tr
    WHERE tr.run_date BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'
),
stop_counts AS (
    -- number of stops per run, used to split run cost equally across stops
    SELECT run_id, COUNT(*) AS n_stops
    FROM run_stops
    GROUP BY run_id
)
SELECT sh.account_manager,
       ROUND(SUM(ra.avoidable / sc.n_stops), 2) AS avoidable_cost_eur,
       COUNT(DISTINCT ra.run_id) AS runs
FROM run_avoidable ra
JOIN run_stops rs ON rs.run_id = ra.run_id
JOIN stop_counts sc ON sc.run_id = ra.run_id
JOIN shippers sh ON sh.shipper_id = rs.shipper_id
GROUP BY sh.account_manager
ORDER BY avoidable_cost_eur DESC;
ai_answer: The three Account Managers whose shippers drove the most avoidable cost in Q3 2026 (1 July to 30 September) are Denis Davies at €21,625.74, Alphonse Durand at €19,988.22, and Angelica Santi at €17,452.26. Avoidable cost counts the full cost of wasted runs plus the ad-hoc premium on ad-hoc runs, with each run's cost shared equally across its stops. After these three, the next highest is Harry Hudson at €6,065.25.

question: How much unplanned volume did we get on bank holidays in 2026, by country?
ai_sql:
WITH daily_actual AS (
    -- aggregate actual volume to shipper x pickup day BEFORE joining (no fan-out)
    SELECT s.shipper_id, tr.run_date AS pickup_date, SUM(s.packages) AS actual_packages
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = s.run_id
    WHERE s.status <> 'Cancelled'
      AND tr.run_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-12-31'
    GROUP BY s.shipper_id, tr.run_date
)
SELECT sh.country,
       SUM(a.actual_packages) AS unplanned_packages,
       COUNT(*) AS shipper_days
FROM daily_actual a
JOIN shippers sh ON sh.shipper_id = a.shipper_id
JOIN holidays h ON h.country = sh.country AND h.holiday_date = a.pickup_date
LEFT JOIN forecasts f ON f.shipper_id = a.shipper_id AND f.forecast_date = a.pickup_date
WHERE f.shipper_id IS NULL
GROUP BY sh.country
ORDER BY unplanned_packages DESC;
ai_answer:
France had the most unplanned volume on bank holidays in 2026, at 3,402 packages across 82 shipper-days. The UK followed with 2,900 packages over 66 shipper-days, then Italy with 2,285 over 54, and Spain with 1,763 over 44.

This counts pickups from January 1 to December 31, 2026, that fell on a holiday in the shipper's own country. It excludes cancelled shipments and includes only shipper-days with no forecast on file.

question: Which shippers missed the +/-10% attainment band for 3+ consecutive weeks?
ai_sql:
WITH daily_actual AS (
    -- aggregate actual volume to shipper x pickup day BEFORE joining (no fan-out)
    SELECT s.shipper_id, tr.run_date AS pickup_date, SUM(s.packages) AS actual_packages
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = s.run_id
    WHERE s.status <> 'Cancelled'
    GROUP BY s.shipper_id, tr.run_date
),
daily AS (
    -- start from forecasts; only days with a forecast row count
    SELECT f.shipper_id, f.forecast_date, f.forecast_packages,
           COALESCE(a.actual_packages, 0) AS actual_packages
    FROM forecasts f
    LEFT JOIN daily_actual a
      ON a.shipper_id = f.shipper_id AND a.pickup_date = f.forecast_date
),
weekly AS (
    SELECT shipper_id,
           date(forecast_date, '-' || strftime('%w', forecast_date) || ' days') AS week_start,
           1.0 * SUM(actual_packages) / SUM(forecast_packages) AS attainment
    FROM daily
    GROUP BY shipper_id, week_start
),
missed AS (
    SELECT shipper_id, week_start, attainment,
           CAST(julianday(week_start) AS INTEGER) AS jd
    FROM weekly
    WHERE attainment < 0.9 OR attainment > 1.1
),
islands AS (
    -- consecutive missed weeks share the same (jd - 7*rn) value
    SELECT shipper_id, week_start, attainment,
           jd - 7 * ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY shipper_id ORDER BY week_start) AS grp
    FROM missed
)
SELECT shipper_id,
       MIN(week_start) AS streak_start,
       MAX(week_start) AS streak_end,
       COUNT(*) AS consecutive_weeks_missed,
       ROUND(100.0 * AVG(attainment), 1) AS avg_attainment_pct
FROM islands
GROUP BY shipper_id, grp
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY consecutive_weeks_missed DESC, shipper_id, streak_start;
ai_answer: The query found 366 streaks of at least 3 consecutive weeks where a shipper's actual packages fell outside the ±10% band of forecast; the first 50 are shown. Twelve shippers (S0013, S0087, S0094, S0115, S0162, S0263, S0369, S0381, S0385, S0525, S0813, S0996) appear with a single 92-week streak from 2024-12-29 to 2026-09-27, averaging about 64–69% of forecast, which may point to a forecast or data problem worth checking. The other shown streaks run 5 to 11 weeks, mostly starting between late 2025 and early 2026, with averages from about 66% to 85%. Cancelled shipments are excluded, weeks run Sunday to Saturday, and only days with a forecast are counted, across all available dates.

question: For milkruns, which shippers are most often the cause of late node arrivals?
ai_sql:
WITH stop_lateness AS (
    SELECT rs.run_id, rs.shipper_id, rs.stop_sequence,
           (strftime('%s', rs.actual_pickup_time) - strftime('%s', rs.planned_pickup_time)) / 60.0 AS lateness_min
    FROM run_stops rs
),
stop_delay AS (
    SELECT run_id, shipper_id, stop_sequence,
           lateness_min - COALESCE(LAG(lateness_min) OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY stop_sequence), 0) AS delay_added
    FROM stop_lateness
),
late_milkruns AS (
    SELECT run_id
    FROM truck_runs
    WHERE run_type = 'milkrun'
      AND run_outcome = 'completed'
      AND actual_arrival_time > planned_arrival_time
),
blamed AS (
    SELECT sd.run_id, sd.shipper_id,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sd.run_id ORDER BY sd.delay_added DESC, sd.stop_sequence) AS rn
    FROM stop_delay sd
    JOIN late_milkruns lm ON lm.run_id = sd.run_id
),
milk_counts AS (
    SELECT rs.shipper_id, COUNT(DISTINCT rs.run_id) AS milkruns
    FROM run_stops rs
    JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = rs.run_id
    WHERE tr.run_type = 'milkrun'
    GROUP BY rs.shipper_id
)
SELECT b.shipper_id,
       s.name,
       COUNT(*) AS late_milkruns_blamed,
       mc.milkruns
FROM blamed b
JOIN milk_counts mc ON mc.shipper_id = b.shipper_id
JOIN shippers s ON s.shipper_id = b.shipper_id
WHERE b.rn = 1
  AND mc.milkruns >= 20
GROUP BY b.shipper_id, s.name, mc.milkruns
ORDER BY late_milkruns_blamed DESC;
ai_answer: Adam 453 is the shipper most often blamed for late milkrun arrivals, with 185 late runs out of its 191 milkruns. The next most frequent are Anichini-Zabarella SPA 579 (178 of 183) and Ferrand 496 (171 of 177). The counts cover all recorded milkruns with no date limit, counting only completed runs that arrived after their planned time, and only shippers with at least 20 milkruns. Each late run is assigned to the stop that added the most delay.
